A.explanation: The stored elastic energy would be the area under the unloading curve Q, not the loop between P and Q.

B.explanation: The cord returns to $x = 0$, so there is no permanent extension and no plastic deformation.

C.explanation: The loop area is work put in minus work recovered, which is energy transferred to internal stores and dissipated as heat.

D.explanation: Work done to extend is the total area under loading path P to the $x$-axis, not just the shaded loop.

hints: Notice the $F$ against $x$ graph has different paths for stretching P and relaxing Q, with a shaded loop between them.
Recall that area under an $F$-$x$ curve represents work done, so compare the larger area under P with the smaller area under Q.
Think about what happens to the missing work when the cord returns to $x = 0$ with less work recovered than was put in.
walkthrough: Identify the axes: area under any $F$ against $x$ curve has units of $\text{N m} = \text{J}$ and represents work done.
For loading along P, work done on the cord by $F$ equals the area between P and the $x$-axis.
For unloading along Q, work done by the cord as $F$ is removed equals the area between Q and the $x$-axis, which is smaller.
Subtract: input work minus recovered work leaves the shaded loop area between P and Q.

Since the loop starts and ends at the origin, there is no permanent extension, so this lost mechanical energy is not stored and not plastic work but is dissipated as heat in the rubber. This is option C.
